sentences.text: Ampelosaurus possessed a long neck and tail like other sauropods and was covered in armor made of osteoderms ranging from 25 to 28 centimeters in length.

The holotype specimen of Ampelosaurus atacis consists of a group of three connected dorsal vertebrae, while a separate scapula was found attached to a coracoid and measured 72 centimeters in length. Le Loeuff identified several distinguishing features for the genus, including weakly spatulate teeth, laterally widening neural spine extremities, a strongly rear-inclining neural arch, a lack of distal scapular expansion, a ventral scapular crest, and plate, bulb, and spine-shaped osteoderms.

The name Ampelosaurus means "vineyard lizard," derived from Greek and Latin roots referencing the Blanquette de Limoux vineyard where it was found. It is the only known species of the fossil genus Ampelosaurus, a titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur.
Fossil evidence of dinosaur eggshells and nests has been found in the same rock layer where Ampelosaurus fossils occur.
This dinosaur exhibited a slower growth rate after its bone microstructure became unique among sauropods.
The genus Ampelosaurus was described by Jean Le Loeuff in 1995, with the type species A. atacis named in the same year.
Over 500 bones discovered since 1989 at the Upper Cretaceous Bellevue locality in southern France have been assigned to Ampelosaurus atacis.

While some remains were recovered from the lower levels of the Marnes Rouges Inférieures Formation, Ampelosaurus atacis is definitively known only from the base of the Marnes de la Maurine Member in the Upper Aude Valley, southwestern France.

Reports of Ampelosaurus remains in the Petites Pyrénées and Chaînon de Saint-Chinian have never been confirmed by a formal publication, and studies have shown that titanosaur teeth found at Cruzy differ from those of Ampelosaurus and belong to a new taxon currently under description.

Ampelosaurus is classified as a moderate-sized titanosaur from the early Maastrichtian of southwestern France. In 2018, Díez Díaz and colleagues placed Ampelosaurus in the clade Lirainosaurinae, grouping it with other French and Spanish titanosaurs from the late Campanian to Maastrichtian. Ampelosaurus belongs to the parent group Lirainosaurinae and is the sister taxon to Atsinganosaurus, and their shared clade is positioned phylogenetically between Saltasauridae and the groups Aeolosaurini or Lognkosauria. It is debated whether there were at least two different titanosaurs in southern France during the Late Cretaceous, as another skull showed some differences.
Ampelosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous Period, specifically the Early Maastrichtian epoch, approximately 71.5 million years ago.

A 2012 study suggested that Bellevue contained three morphotypes of titanosaurs, with one tentatively assigned to the genus Lirainosaurus, creating debate over species attribution. Researchers in 2021 agreed that a second titanosaur species existed at Bellevue but suggested it was more similar to the genus Garrigatitan. Recent studies indicate that the diagnosis of Ampelosaurus will need to be revised due to the presence of additional titanosaur species at the site. Recent studies suggest that many bones previously assigned to Ampelosaurus belong to a distinct species, potentially requiring the description of a new titanosaur and an emended diagnosis for Ampelosaurus.
